mys-m11-2.prompt: How was Peter being held that night?
options: Sleeping between two soldiers, bound with two chains
Alone in a pit sealed with a stone
Standing in stocks in the inner prison
Locked in a tower with no guards inside
mys-m11-2.hint: Acts 12:6 describes how Peter lay that night and what the keepers were doing.

extra.clue: Guard report: On the night before Herod planned to bring the prisoner out, the cell was under full watch, with keepers stationed before the door.

mys-m11-4.prompt: Who was this witness, and at whose house did it happen?
options: Lydia, at the house of Simon the tanner
Priscilla, at the house of Jason
Dorcas, at the house of Cornelius
Rhoda, at the house of Mary the mother of John Mark
mys-m11-4.hint: Acts 12:12-13 names both the house and the damsel who came to the gate.

extra.clue: Witness statement: a young woman at a house where many were gathered praying came to hearken when someone knocked at the gate. She knew the voice, but for gladness she ran inside instead of opening it.

mys-m3-1.prompt: According to the text, what was Laban doing when the images were taken?
options: He was at a wedding feast in Haran
He had gone to shear his sheep
He was offering a sacrifice on mount Gilead
He was digging a well in Gerar
mys-m3-1.hint: Genesis 31:19 says where Laban had gone.

extra.clue: Household log: the master of the house was away when the images vanished, and Jacob left without telling him.

mys-m4-2.prompt: Where were the two men actually hidden?
options: At the bottom of a well
In a cave outside the city
On the roof, under stalks of flax
In the king's own storehouse
mys-m4-2.hint: Joshua 2:6 tells where she had brought them.

extra.clue: Statement given to the king's messengers: 'There came men unto me, but I wist not whence they were... pursue after them quickly.' Yet the text says she had already taken the two men and hid them.

mys-m4-1.prompt: According to the record, who sent the two men out to spy?
options: Moses the servant of the LORD
The king of Jericho
Rahab
Joshua the son of Nun
mys-m4-1.hint: The answer is in the first verse of Joshua 2.

extra.clue: Camp record: two men departed from Shittim under orders to view the land, even Jericho. It was later told the king that they had come in to the house of a woman named Rahab.

mys-m4-3.prompt: Which way did the pursuers go in search of the men?
options: North to the mountain of Lebanon
The way to Jordan unto the fords
Toward the Red sea
Back to Shittim
mys-m4-3.hint: Joshua 2:7 names the way they went.

extra.clue: City record: the king's men went out in pursuit of the spies, and as soon as the pursuers had gone out, the city gate was shut behind them.

mys-m6-3.prompt: When Delilah first asked, what did Samson say would make him weak?
options: Being kept from eating bread and drinking water
Being bound with seven green withs that were never dried
Having his eyes put out
Being bound with chains of iron

extra.clue: Evidence report: men had been lying in wait in Delilah's chamber. When she bound Samson and cried that the Philistines were upon him, he broke the bonds as a thread of tow breaks when it touches the fire.

mys-m6-4.prompt: What secret did Samson finally reveal to Delilah?
options: That he could be weakened only if he were bound while asleep
That he would lose his strength if he ever drank wine
That his strength came from a hidden amulet he wore
That no razor had come upon his head, for he had been a Nazarite unto God from his mother's womb
mys-m6-4.hint: Judges 16:17 records what he finally told her.

extra.clue: Witness statement: "She pressed him daily with her words, until his soul was vexed unto death. Then he finally told her all his heart."

mys-m7-1.prompt: According to the first woman, what was the living arrangement of the two women?

They dwelt together in one house
They were traveling strangers who met at an inn

extra.clue: Court record: two women came to the king and stood before him, and the first woman began her testimony.

mys-m9-1.prompt: For what price did Judas Iscariot covenant with the chief priests?

wis-w1-7.prompt: You agreed to sell your car to a neighbour at a set price and shook hands on it. Before the transfer, someone else offers you considerably more. Which response best reflects the character described in Psalms 15:4?
options: Invent a mechanical problem so you can back out gracefully
Keep your word to the neighbour even though it now costs you
Tell the neighbour they must match the new price or lose the deal
Accept the higher offer, since nothing has been signed yet
wis-w1-7.hint: Think about what it means to swear "to his own hurt, and change not."

wis-w2-2.prompt: Scrolling social media, you see friends showing off vacations and new homes, and you start feeling dissatisfied with your modest apartment. You catch yourself planning purchases just to keep up. What does Hebrews 13:5 counsel here?
options: Contentment only comes once you own as much as your neighbors
Keep up with others so you don't feel left behind
Be content with what you have, trusting that God will never leave you
Envy is harmless as long as you don't say it out loud
wis-w2-2.hint: Hebrews 13:5 begins with a word about covetousness.

wis-w7-2.prompt: Your manager hints that layoffs might come sometime next year. You start spending every evening imagining worst-case scenarios months ahead, and it is draining your joy today. What does Jesus counsel in Matthew 6:34?

Ask God to tell you exactly what will happen next year before you let yourself rest
Push the worry down and tell yourself your job is certainly safe
Take no anxious thought for tomorrow, and give today's strength to today

wis-w8-1.prompt: A coworker has openly mocked you in meetings and spread unkind rumors about you. A friend suggests you quietly return the favor or at least cut them off entirely. Which response best reflects the teaching of Matthew 5:44?
options: Ignore them completely until they apologize first
Love them, bless them, do good to them and pray for them
Return the treatment in kind so they learn a lesson
Gather evidence and expose their faults to the whole team
wis-w8-1.hint: Matthew 5:44 gives Jesus' command about enemies.

wis-w8-2.prompt: You help greet people at a community gathering. A well-dressed businessman and a visibly poor man in worn clothes arrive at the same time, and you feel tempted to give the businessman the best seat. What does James 2:1-4 counsel here?
options: Let the poor man in only if there are seats left over
Show no partiality, welcoming both with equal honor
Seat the businessman up front, since he may support the group
Ask the poor man to stand at the back so others feel comfortable
wis-w8-2.hint: James 2:1-4 describes a man with a gold ring and a poor man in vile raiment.

wis-w8-8.prompt: A rival at work who treated you unfairly has just been publicly reprimanded and demoted. Colleagues invite you to celebrate their downfall over lunch. Which response best reflects the teaching of Proverbs 24:17-18?
options: Smile inwardly but avoid saying anything publicly
Celebrate, since justice has finally been done
Refuse to rejoice in their fall, guarding even your heart from gladness at it
Remind everyone of what they did so the lesson sticks
wis-w8-8.hint: Proverbs 24:18 explains why this matters to the LORD.

Stop talking to the friend who criticised you

Avoid all friendships so no one can influence you
